method.workload: One unchanged compiled INT8 decoder tile, tile_batch=4, using a previously cached FP16 encoder latent; capture layers 0,17,35.
method.capture_correction: Initial capture hooked opt.decoder_fused_qk_rope, while runtime uses flat decoder_fused_qk_rope. Zero actual hits caused the required failure. The corrected capture binds the runtime module, observes 36 calls, and matches the unhooked tile exactly. Failed capture is retained and contributes no performance samples.
method.layout_comparison: Two producer layouts; actual identical Torch Flash kernel verified without fallback. Chain timing includes preparation/packing, Flash, nan_to_num, output reshape and INT8 projection, with fresh outputs.
method.native_comparison: Native M128 is an exact-output anchor against Torch. The sole candidate changes M128 to M64 with FP16/D64/N128/W4 fixed. Current CUDA stream, NaN write sentinels and downstream projection exactness are checked. Output/LSE allocations remain in per-call timing.
method.sampling: For each layer and candidate, 6 alternating ABBA/BAAB local blocks; each sample averages 10 calls. Samples are repeated local measurements, not independent full-video trials.
method.timing_scope: Validation, Torch profiler dispatch checks, compilation, loading and tensor capture are excluded. No profiler observer is used inside timed samples.

interpretation_limits: All three-layer layout and native candidates passed numerical gates but were slower; no candidate was promoted to full decode.

The native M128/M64 register, shared-memory, stack and spill records describe the independently compiled experiment library. In particular M128 40-byte stack / 72-byte spill stores / 60-byte spill loads are ptxas reports for this experiment, NOT measured spill traffic of the original Torch kernel.
The prior Nsight Systems Torch kernel metadata reported 255 registers/thread and 49152 shared-memory bytes. It did not establish occupancy, bandwidth utilization or actual spill traffic.
The independent M64 build used 166 registers with no compiler-reported spill, yet measured local latency regressed. Resource reductions are not performance proof.
Native M128 uses the matching FA2 kernel template and returns exact results, but its ctypes launch wrapper differs from Torch dispatch and adds host overhead; its local chain remained close to Torch.
Existing offline FlashAttention and CUTLASS sources are BSD-3-Clause; no new source download or global installation was required.
